modern: As your habitual thoughts are, so too will be the character of your mind; for the soul is dyed by its thoughts. Dye it, then, with a continuous series of thoughts such as these: for instance, that where a man can live, there he can also live well. But he must live in a palace; well then, he can also live well in a palace. And again, consider that whatever purpose each thing has been made for, it has been made for this, and it is carried towards this; and its end lies in that towards which it is carried; and where the end is, there too is the advantage and the good of each thing. Now the good for the rational animal is society; for it has been shown above that we are made for society. Is it not plain that the inferior exists for the sake of the superior? But things which have life are superior to those which do not, and of those which have life the superior are those which have reason.

explained.summary:
Your mind takes on the colour of what you usually think about, the way cloth takes on dye. So soak it in good thoughts. One is that you can live well wherever you have to live, even in a palace, which for Marcus was not a fantasy but his daily life.

Another is that everything is made for a purpose and finds its good in that purpose. For beings who can reason, that purpose is living with and for others. The higher kinds of life, he argues, are the ones that reason, and reasoning creatures are made for each other.
explained.today: What you scroll through on the train, the podcasts you play and the grumbles you repeat to yourself all shape the person you’re becoming. Someone who rehearses grievances all day will find it hard to be cheerful at dinner.
